epsin_ccs.case: high-tension CCS flat->dome->Omega; mechanism per user-provided plan (Joseph et al. 2020 Comm Biol, user's own paper)
epsin_ccs.reasoning_trace: Target mean curvature H=0.03 nm^-1 at high tension sigma=0.03 kBT/nm^2 requires c_eff ~ 2*H = 0.06 nm^-1. Since tension gates the wedge (ENTH) term down significantly at this sigma (above the tension_half_kBT_nm2 chosen), the wedge alone contributes a reduced effective c0. To reach c_eff~0.06 nm^-1 we lean heavily on near-saturating IDP crowding (c_max=0.045, coverage=0.85) plus a coat with moderate rigidity (3.5) and a small intrinsic curvature (0.005 nm^-1) from partial lattice ordering, concentrating both wedge and crowd contributions on the 11310 nm^2 patch. Since both wedge+coat and crowding+coat are known synergistic (coat concentrates the driving curvature generators), a coupling_correction of 0.25 is applied to capture the super-additive effect needed to reach dome/Omega morphology at this elevated tension. || [wedge→c0_plus_kappa_softening] Epsin ENTH domain wedge insertion gives a moderate intrinsic curvature contribution, but at sigma=0.03 kBT/nm^2 (above tension_half of 0.02) the tension-gating softens its effective contribution substantially, so it alone cannot reach target. || [crowding→saturating_surface_pressure] CCS (epsin C-terminal disordered region) tails are densely packed on the coat patch; near-saturating coverage (0.85, well past phi_half) drives strong entropic crowding pressure to compensate for the tension-softened wedge term. || [coat→rigidity_area_constraint] AP2/clathrin lattice over the 11310 nm^2 patch concentrates both wedge and crowding contributions and adds modest rigidity plus a small intrinsic curvature from partial lattice maturation, helping push toward dome/Omega stage. || [tension→constant_tension_frame] Case-fixed high membrane tension of 0.03 kBT/nm^2, which gates down the wedge contribution and necessitates compensation via crowding and coat rigidity. || coupling_correction=0.25 (coat concentrates wedge/crowd → >additive synergy) || Target mean curvature H=0.03 nm^-1 at high tension sigma=0.03 kBT/nm^2 requires c_eff ~ 2*H = 0.06 nm^-1. Since tension gates the wedge (ENTH) term down significantly at this sigma (above the tension_half_kBT_nm2 chosen), the wedge alone contributes a reduced effective c0. To reach c_eff~0.06 nm^-1 we lean heavily on near-saturating IDP crowding (c_max=0.045, coverage=0.85) plus a coat with moderate rigidity (3.5) and a small intrinsic curvature (0.005 nm^-1) from partial lattice ordering, concentrating both wedge and crowd contributions on the 11310 nm^2 patch. Since both wedge+coat and crowding+coat are known synergistic (coat concentrates the driving curvature generators), a coupling_correction of 0.25 is applied to capture the super-additive effect needed to reach dome/Omega morphology at this elevated tension.

players.justification: Epsin ENTH domain wedge insertion gives a moderate intrinsic curvature contribution, but at sigma=0.03 kBT/nm^2 (above tension_half of 0.02) the tension-gating softens its effective contribution substantially, so it alone cannot reach target.

CCS (epsin C-terminal disordered region) tails are densely packed on the coat patch; near-saturating coverage (0.85, well past phi_half) drives strong entropic crowding pressure to compensate for the tension-softened wedge term.

AP2/clathrin lattice over the 11310 nm^2 patch concentrates both wedge and crowding contributions and adds modest rigidity plus a small intrinsic curvature from partial lattice maturation, helping push toward dome/Omega stage.
Case-fixed high membrane tension of 0.03 kBT/nm^2, which gates down the wedge contribution and necessitates compensation via crowding and coat rigidity.

complementarity_test.claim: Neither ENTH/H0 wedge nor IDP crowding alone crosses the Omega threshold; both + multivalent coat required. Mechanism as described in the user-provided plan (Joseph et al. 2020, user's own paper); reproduced qualitatively, not quantitatively validated.

provenance_note: Joseph et al. 2020 (Commun Biol) is the user's own paper, named in the attached sprint plan. Joseph et al. 2022, Membranes 12(9):859 (doi:10.3390/membranes12090859) is a real related paper supplied by the user (not named in the plan). The pipeline reproduces the QUALITATIVE MECHANISM (ENTH+IDP complementarity; spherical/filamentous H0-dependence); it was NOT quantitatively validated against those papers' measured data, which are not in hand this sprint.
